texts: Senior Software Engineer & System Architect · Node.js · NestJS · Angular · Multi-Tenant ERP
5+ years building multi-tenant SaaS platforms. Full-stack engineer on the EasyRes B2B/B2C travel marketplace since 2022, and creator of
, an industrial ERP and workforce OS — owned from architecture to production.

Senior Software Engineer & System Architect with 5+ years of experience in two worlds: high-scale multi-tenant travel SaaS, and complex distributed systems and ERPs. I deliver end to end — from architecture and data model to production deployment.

Works across Node.js, NestJS, Angular, TypeScript, MongoDB, Redis, Docker and AWS EC2, with a deep understanding of system design, microservices, API integration and performance. As Principal System Architect & Product Creator of OpsX (opsx.in), designed edge-first attendance, geofencing, RBAC and automated payroll for Indian SMEs.

At EasyRes Travel Technologies (since 2022) I am a full-stack engineer on a multi-tenant B2B/B2C travel marketplace — the top contributor to its Angular consumer and admin portals, with about 3,000 commits across 24 repositories. I built the B2B agent portal, created the travel-insurance and Via.com ferry microservices, and integrated suppliers and payments including 2GO, Barkota, Starlite Ferries, RateHawk, Via Hotels, Jayride and Xendit.

I care about money-safe booking flows (atomic wallet claims, automatic reversals, a 138-check offline test harness), financial accuracy (OpsX posts payroll to a double-entry ledger in PostgreSQL), and code reviews — I have merged 480+ pull requests, including teammates' and release branches. I ship faster with AI coding assistants (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) for boilerplate, test scaffolding and query tuning, while reviewing and testing every change myself.

EasyRes Travel Technologies Pvt. Ltd., Delhi · Jul 2024 – Present

Full-stack engineer on a multi-tenant B2B/B2C travel marketplace with a subscriber, agency and agent hierarchy, built as 20+ Node.js microservices, one per product; ~3,000 commits across 24 repositories since 2022.

Platform integrations: flights via Travelport and Sabre GDS and the Atlas LCC aggregator, searched in parallel; hotels via RateHawk, GRN Connect, Dida, Bedsonline and Via Hotels; ferries via 2GO, Barkota, Starlite Ferries and Via; airport transfers via Jayride; payments via Xendit and PayMongo; plus in-house holiday packages, tours and visa with no third-party supplier.

Client-facing ownership: work directly with client stakeholders to gather requirements, plan features and design technical solutions for ferries, hotels, visa, holiday packages, airport shuttles and payments (Xendit, PayMongo), then own delivery end to end.

Round trips on one-way supplier APIs: Barkota and 2GO offer no native round-trip booking, so I designed round trips on top of their single-journey APIs — outbound and return searched separately and priced together, one gateway or wallet payment covering both legs, two supplier reservations tracked leg by leg. 2GO has no cancel, void or release endpoint, so the design validates both legs fully before any seat is held, books each leg while persisting state, and records unreleasable holds for follow-up.

Ferries (2GO, Barkota, Starlite, Via): full supplier integration plus client-specific rules — built the Via.com ferry service from scratch (search, seat block, payment, booking, restart-safe status polling); 2GO's new B2C API with restricted fares (senior, PWD, student, minor) and per-agency round-trip permissions; the whole B2B channel for Barkota; Starlite refunds, voids, ticketing and Xendit notifications.

Designed money-safe booking flows that prevent double charges: atomic claims before every wallet or supplier side effect, automatic wallet reversal on failed bookings and a manual-review queue for unknown outcomes — proven by a 138-check offline test harness (in-memory database, mocked suppliers, real HTTP routers) and a ferry round-trip regression suite.

Hotels: turned client requirements into the RateHawk integration as its main contributor (booking finish/status, order info, cancellation penalties) with an hourly cron archiving supplier logs to AWS S3; Via Hotels per-tenant credentials, dynamic emails and a grade-code pricing fix.

In-house products with no third-party supplier: built and run visa processing and holiday/tour packages end to end around client needs — visa modules on the visa service I set up, and packages with tenant-managed suppliers, activities, prices and currencies (140+ backend commits).

Airport shuttles and insurance: Jayride integration shaped by client use cases (booking list, details, wallet payment, redirects); created the travel-insurance microservice end to end (quotes, policies, gateway and wallet booking).

Payments, pricing and flights: integrated Xendit end to end (hosted sessions, webhooks, per-tenant config) and worked on the PayMongo checkout; email-OTP two-step login; grade codes plus agency markups and discounts across products, multi-currency precision, agent and agency management; Angular flight search and booking over Travelport, Sabre and Atlas fares.

Engineering practice: merged 480+ pull requests, including teammates' and release/hot-fix branches; mentor to junior developers; Claude Code and GitHub Copilot for boilerplate, test scaffolding and query tuning, with every change reviewed and tested.

Architected edge-first attendance: offline SQLite queue with batch sync and on-device face verification on kiosk tablets.

Run it in production on AWS EC2: rolling restarts across two API instances, BullMQ workers on Redis, nginx.

Multi-tenant SaaS ERP for Indian SMEs and plants: attendance, payroll, field staff, factory kiosk, procurement and stock. Designed, built and operated end to end.
Edge computing: offline-first SQLite queue on Android devices with store-and-forward batch sync, and on-device face verification on kiosk tablets — no image leaves the device.
Geofenced attendance and field tracking: GPS geofences, live map, trips and proof of delivery.

Full Stack Engineer — private company platform

A travel SaaS where subscribers run their own agencies and agents: flights, hotels, ferries, holiday packages, tours, visa, insurance and airport transfers, with white-label consumer portals for client brands.

20+ Node.js microservices, one per product, behind a gateway; supplier integrations including Travelport and Sabre GDS, the Atlas LCC aggregator, RateHawk, GRN Connect, Dida, Bedsonline, Via Hotels, 2GO, Barkota, Starlite Ferries, Via.com ferries, Jayride, Xendit and PayMongo; in-house packages, tours and visa.
Booking lifecycle: search, pricing, seat block/hold, wallet or gateway payment, ticketing, polling, cancellation, refunds and PDF vouchers.
Wallet safety: atomic claims, automatic reversal on failed supplier bookings and a manual-review path — backed by a 138-check offline test harness.
Multi-level pricing: subscriber grade codes plus agency markups and discounts per product.
Lets a business collect payments straight into its own bank account through a UPI QR code, without a payment gateway's per-transaction fee, for OpsX invoices and gym membership fees.

Trust model: the payer's UTR (UPI transaction reference) is treated as a claim, never as proof. Every confirmation path goes through one compare-and-set approval (claimed → approved) that reverts on failure.
Each UTR counts once: a unique partial index on {tenant, UTR}; rejecting or voiding a payment releases the UTR instead of deleting the evidence.

Bank-statement reconciliation: upload a statement (HDFC, SBI, Kotak, Axis formats), see a dry run first, then approve every matched claim in one step (matching by amount and day in IST), get one-to-one match suggestions for unclaimed credits, and see contradictions flagged (e.g. one bank credit named by two claims) instead of silently rejecting them.
Reproduced a double-approval race with failing tests before fixing it (claim-first findOneAndUpdate, 409 when the payment changed underneath).

Scoped deliberately: no scraping of payment apps and no OTP-linking of merchant accounts, for terms-of-service and payment-aggregator licensing reasons. Next steps: a gateway adapter and bank-alert parsing.
Clinic Queue — Real-time Token & Queue SaaS
Clinic check-in, live token queue, prescriptions and patient alerts, with a super-admin panel and an Android app.
Transactional outbox on Postgres (LISTEN/NOTIFY + SKIP LOCKED workers) drives WhatsApp/SMS alerts with expiry, state re-check and SMS fallback.
Live queue over Socket.IO; deploy kit with systemd, nginx and rollback. Built and deploy-ready.
SOS, live location sharing with trusted contacts, a Safe Walk timer and family pairing.
The server escalates automatically when a timed check-in is missed, using BullMQ delayed jobs.
Live location over Socket.IO; 27 integration tests in CI. Working prototype.
Content Automation Platform — Video, Podcast & Social Publishing
Personal · runs daily as scheduled jobs
A set of scheduled pipelines that turn one piece of content into YouTube videos, a podcast feed and posts on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and X, built to survive restarts, quotas and duplicate runs.

Resumable multi-stage pipeline (script, voice, images, render, scheduled upload): each stage checkpoints to disk, so a closed laptop or a quota error resumes where it stopped instead of starting over.

No duplicate uploads: a shared schedule ledger written by three jobs, guarded by an O_EXCL lockfile with stale-lock breaking, plus a channel-ID check before every upload. Resumable 8 MB chunked uploads with YouTube's publishAt scheduling.

Idempotent fan-out to four social platforms from RSS, sitemap and video sources: a dedup ledger keyed platform:brand:source:id with atomic temp-file-and-rename writes, a 'baseline on first sight' rule that prevents a backfill flood, and a dry-run mode.

Platform specifics handled in code: Meta Reels resumable upload with container-status polling, X OAuth 1.0a signed by hand, LinkedIn as organisation or member, and a self-hosted podcast RSS on Cloudflare R2 (Spotify has no upload API).
65 automated tests across the two pipelines.
Pro-bono website for an NGO in 14 Indian languages (including English and Hindi), with light and dark themes.
